messages:
Anna (Support): Hey team — customer `acme-inc` opened an escalation: getting a surge of 429s and auth failures starting ~09:12 UTC. They say tokens are valid. Also seeing a billing spike. Pasting the log snippet they sent:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: req_01F3...
tenant-id: acme-inc
error: rate_limiter: auth_throttle_exceeded
retry-after: 30
```

Can someone triage? Customer is blocked (product search) and is asking for ETA.

Raj (SRE): @Anna thanks — can you drop the full headers (redact tokens) and the request pattern (paths, qps)? Also did we have any limiter config deploys in the last hour?

Anna (Support): Pasted headers (redacted):
```
method: POST
path: /v1/generate
host: api.redwood.example
content-type: application/json
authorization: Bearer <redacted>
x-tenant-id: acme-inc
x-request-id: req_01F3...
```
Pattern: spikes of fan-out from their web tier — ~350 rps over 30s windows then normalizes. They say they only retried once.

Leo (Runtime): I see a config PR merged ~09:05 (PR #4823) that changed limiter defaults for new tenants. Deploy bot shows it rolled at 09:08. @Raj could be related.

Deploy Bot: PR #4823 merged by @dev-elena and deployed to staging and prod at 2029-09-20T09:08:14Z.

Raj (SRE): Ok looking at metrics for tenant `acme-inc` — token-bucket drain rate is normal but refill metric shows near-zero refill (0.0008 tokens/s) starting at 09:08. That's effectively making bursts collapse. Taking a quick snapshot of limiter config for that tenant: 
```
{ "burst_window": 0, "refill_unit": "ms", "refill_rate": 1 }
```
If burst_window=0 we treat it as no burst allowance -> every request consumes immediate tokens with no windowed restoration. That would explain 429s.

Maria (Product): That would match the customer experience. But why did burst_window become 0? Was that intended as a default?

Leo (Runtime): PR #4823 changed the defaults to unify tenant templates. Looks like a logic bug: an environment var was read as a string and `parseInt('')` returned 0 for tenants that didn't opt-in, so burst_window defaulted to 0. The change slipped through because we had no unit tests around template defaults.

Anna (Support): Customer wants a short-term fix now. Can we restore previous behavior for `acme-inc`?

Raj (SRE): Immediate mitigations I can do: 1) bump their tenant burst_window to 60s via the admin API, 2) add a soft override to treat burst_window<=1 as '60' for managed tenants in the rate limiter (hotfix), 3) rollback PR #4823 if hotfix risky. Which route do we prefer?

Leo (Runtime): Hotfix + per-tenant override is fastest (no full rollback). I can push a small patch that treats burst_window<=0 as missing and uses previous default (30000 ms). It should be safe.

Raj (SRE): I'll also open a temporary quota increase for `acme-inc` to remove immediate customer impact while patch rolls.

Maria (Product): Please communicate ETA to customer: ETA 15–30m for hotfix + 5m for admin bump. I'll draft the message: "We identified a config defaults regression causing burst allowance to be set to zero for some tenants. We're applying a fix and temporarily increasing your throughput. Will follow up with a permanent patch and postmortem."

Anna (Support): I'll send that now and CC you all.

Deploy Bot: Hotfix branch `limiter-fallback-4823` created by @leo and deployed to canary at 2029-09-20T09:22:50Z.

Raj (SRE): Patch applied to all limiter pods, restarted service. I bumped `acme-inc` burst_window to 30000 ms via admin API at 09:25:10Z. Their 429s dropped immediately in metrics. Billing spike telemetry normalized.

Anna (Support): Customer confirmed reduced 429s and traffic returning to normal. They appreciate the quick turnaround but want root cause details and an RCA.

Leo (Runtime): Root cause summary (short): PR #4823 introduced a change that reads optional template fields incorrectly; missing values parsed as 0 -> burst_window = 0 for some tenants. No unit tests covered missing-field behavior.

Raj (SRE): Post-incident action items I propose: 
- Revert PR #4823 until full test coverage and migration scripts are added. (Owner: @leo, ETA: EOW)
- Add lint/protections in template parser to reject invalid burst_window/refill_unit values. (Owner: @leo, ETA: 3 days)
- Add an alert that fires when refill_rate < 0.01 tokens/s for any active tenant. (Owner: @raj, ETA: 48h)
- Hotfix: treat burst_window<=0 as missing for managed tenants (merged). (Owner: @leo, done)
- Customer follow-up and RCA doc. (Owner: @maria, ETA: 2 business days)

Maria (Product): SGTM. I'll start the RCA doc and schedule a short sync with customer next week.

Anna (Support): Posting final note to customer and will keep the case open until RCA is shared. Thanks everyone :thumbsup: :eyes:

Raj (SRE): Adding postmortem tag and creating incident page. Will include timelines and metric graphs.

Leo (Runtime): I'll open PRs for parser tests and the revert.

Anna (Support): Closing the escalation in support UI but keeping Slack thread pinned for the RCA.

[thread end]
